newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ADRS buoyed by high tech, await Fed.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ADRS buoyed by high tech, await Fed.

text.p: Foreign stocks were steady in New York on Tuesday ahead of a Federal Reserve interest rate meeting, buoyed by overseas electronics shares and the Netherlands' Akzo Nobel N.V. drug company, analysts said.

Jorge Mariscal, chief strategist for Goldman Sachs, said Latin American stocks were largely firm as investors priced in a rate increase from the Federal Open Market Committee. The panel is expected to announce its decision at 1415 EDT/1815 GMT.
"This is one of the most anticipated rate increases in a long time and the real surprise is if there is no increase at all," he said.

Mariscal added that most analysts expected a boost of 25 basis points in short-term interest rates. Most trade in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) from Latin America was focused on big-capital companies, such as telecommunications and cement, or other blue chips.

Brazil's state telecommunications company Telebras rose 7/8 to 80-5/8 following news its January-to-August net income increasedto 511 million reais from 148 million reais in the same period a year ago.
Morgan Stanley also issued a buy recommendation for Telebras' common stock.

Some foreign electronics stocks moved higher, pulled along by strength in U.S. high-tech and semi-conductor stocks. SGS-Thomson Microelectronics N.V. was up 2-7/8 to 49-1/2 at midday, and Philips N.V. rose 3/8 to 35-7/8.
The Netherland's Akzo Nobel N.V. jumped 1-1/4 to 58-1/2 on news of positive trials of its anti-depressant drug Remeron.
